To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the carried loads and the mean queue lengths are smaller in the integrated model compared to the separated models, and that the carried load and the mean queue length are larger in the quasi-separation model than in the integrated model.
a bandwidth ratio effect appears in the carried load, and a quasi-separation effect appears in the queue lengths.

the system performance can be improved if the bandwidth ratio between narrowband and broadband customers is chosen properly, that is, if the bandwidth is divided in such a way that the number of broadband users is smaller than that of narrowband users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the performance of an integrated broadband communication system.
the development of an analytical method to determine the carried load and the mean queue length of an IBCN queueing system with a finite number of narrowband and broadband sources.
the design of an Integrated Broadband Communications System, which is capable of serving both narrowband and broadband customers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the separated model is not a very good approximation to the multidimensional model, and that it can be used only for rough estimations.
the bandwidth allocation strategy proposed in this paper performs better than the separated models.
the bandwidth allocation strategy is very sensitive to the number of sources of each type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the bandwidth-ratio effect is more dominant than quasi-separation.
the system with separated queues is a good approximation of the original system for the case when the number of sources for each customer type is large.
a bandwidth-ratio of 1.0 gives the best results, and that for a given number of sources, the carried load increases with the number of customers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bandwidth allocation strategy is very sensitive to the traffic mix.
a bandwidth allocation policy can be derived from the model.
, in a system with a finite number of broadband sources, a bandwidth-ratio strategy is better than a quasirandom strategy.
